groups.problem: ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit, but wire.go still registers it as a provider, so wire generation and dependency injection break.
groups.rationale: Both point at the same signature change and the same stale wire.go entries, and suggest the same fix.

groups.problem: The device-limit count and the insert are separate, non-atomic steps, so concurrent new devices can push the count past the limit.
groups.rationale: Same lines, same race condition and the same conditional INSERT fix.

groups.problem: TagDevice now runs synchronously on the request context instead of in a background goroutine, so DB latency blocks anonymous requests and request cancellation aborts tagging.
groups.rationale: Both report that moving tagging from async to sync adds latency and ties tagging to request cancellation. S7 also mentions how the limit error reaches the client, but in the context of the same change.
